articleTitle: Automatic PMD and chromatic dispersion compensation in high capacity transmission
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: PMD and chromatic dispersion introduce problems to be solved for the realization of high capacity optical transmission systems. Aspects of DWDM systems with automatic and simultaneous compensation of PMD and chromatic dispersion are discussed.

articleTitle: Measurements of PMD in the installed fiber plant of Deutsche Telekom
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: In this paper, PMD measurements that were carried out in the installed fiber plant of Deutsche Telekom, which consists solely of G.652 fiber, are presented. The measurements are performed all over Germany during the last three years on nearly 10,000 fiber sections whereby these fiber cables were installed from 1985 to 2001. It should be noted that pre-1994 cables PMD was not yet specified by cable manufacturers and PMD specification were only added around 1995. Fibers with lowest PMD were identified and reserved for high capacity transmission. The data indicate that no direct correlation of the first-order PMD coefficient value with the rollout of the PMD specification by the fiber and cable manufacturers is feasible. Even for cables which were installed during 1985 till 1991 a reasonable number of fibers is suitable for 40 Gbit/s transmission. For 10 Gbit/s selected fibers are used, thus PMD does not impose any limitations and therefore avoiding expensive exchange of fibers.

articleTitle: Precision calibration of an optically sampled analog-to-digital converter
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: The general configuration of the proposed high-speed ADC was described. A train of optical pulses samples the analog signal applied to the optical modulator. A dual-output Mach-Zehnder electro-optic modulator is used to implement phase-encoded optical sampling. Output circuits detect and integrate the modulated optical pulses. The integrated level is held until electronic digitizer converts the signal into digital form. The circuit then resets and waits for the next input pulse. The output circuits include amplifiers before the digitizers.

articleTitle: Field PMD measurements through a commercial, Raman-amplified ULH transmission system
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: Detailed PMD measurements on a field-deployed 986 km commercial system find anomalous PMD contributions of approximately 0.6 ps/node beyond that of the transmission fiber. Dramatic changes in the PMD spectrum due to temperature sensitive components were observed.

articleTitle: Low refractive-index-contrast Fresnel-microstructure fibre for coupling between SMF and photonic crystals
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: A method is described to efficiently couple light between single-mode fibre (SMF) and photonic crystals (PhCs) using a novel Fresnel-zone (FZ) MSF lens. In this study, the proposed FZ-MSF lens focuses light in a similar way to a graded-index (GRIN) rod lens, but instead of having a continuous parabolic refractive index variation, the MSF employs longitudinal FZs to focus light from SMF down to PhC dimensions, and vice-versa. Details on the equations describing the trajectory of a light ray in a medium with spatially-varying refractive index is also discussed.

articleTitle: Multicanonical Monte Carlo of first- and second-order PMD
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: It is shown in this paper that the multicanonical Monte Carlo method can be used to simultaneously compute first- and second-order polarization mode dispersion (PMD) statistics, demonstrating that it has the potential to produce results similar to those obtained with importance sampling.

articleTitle: Laser phase noise degradation from thermal effects due to pump power fluctuations
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: Modelocked Ti:sapphire phase noise below 10 kHz is shown to be susceptible to pump power fluctuations which lead to time-varying thermal changes in the gain medium and exhibit 1/f dependence in the noise transfer function.

articleTitle: Emulation and inversion of polarization mode dispersion
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: Elements of higher-order differential dispersion represent pure higher-order polarization mode dispersion (PMD). They can be applied to the inversion of PMD vector data to determine the fiber pulse's response, and to PMD emulation and compensation.

articleTitle: Exact, agile, optical frequency synthesis using an optical comb generator and optical injection phase lock loop
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: A novel optical source for use in agile dense wavelength division multiplexing (DWDM) networks is described. This source combines reference limited stability, wide tuning range, high spectral purity, narrow line width and fast wavelength switching.

articleTitle: Fast multi-wavelength polarimeter for polarization mode dispersion compensation systems
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: A multi-wavelength polarimeter has been developed for measuring the complete state of polarization of over 100 wavelengths in parallel within 1 millisecond.

articleTitle: PMD of installed fiber - an overview
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: Polarization mode dispersion (PMD) of installed fiber are studied. Data from a standard high-fiber count, buried, ducted cable of recent vintage (c. 1999) NZ-DSF fiber (True Wave Reduced Slope) are presented. This includes long-term measurements from interferometric and wavelength-scanned techniques as well as a new in-situ technique. Some of the challenges for PMD are also discussed.

articleTitle: Multicanonical Monte-Carlo simulations applied to PMD
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: Multicanonical Monte-Carlo simulations are applied to polarization mode dispersion (PMD) statistics of optical fibers in communication systems.

articleTitle: All-order PMD emulator with tunable statistics
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: In this paper, a new configuration is proposed that can emulate all-order polarization mode dispersion (PMD) with tunable statistics. The emulator is composed of multiple birefringent crystals separated with magnetooptic (MO) rotators. Unver certain control conditions, these MO rotators can also work as switches, i.e. they can add or cancel the differential group delay (DGD) between adjacent sections by aligning fast axis with either fast axis of slow axis. Thus the emulator can be configured into different crystal combinations with different birefringence and generate PMD with tunable average values. Computer simulations show the effectiveness of the approach with three typical PMD values as well as demonstrating the corresponding 2nd-order PMD.

articleTitle: Planar waveguide devices for PNM analysis and compensation
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: Compact integrated devices for real-time PMD measurement and novel filter structures that provide emulation and compensation functionality will be discussed that are based on tunable ring resonators and allpass filters.

articleTitle: Experimental demonstration of evanescent coupling from optical fiber tapers to photonic crystal waveguides
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: Experimental results demonstrating nearly-complete mode-selective coupling to photonic crystal waveguides from optical fiber tapers are presented. 98% power transfer with a 20 nm bandwidth, and an effective coupling length of 20 /spl mu/m is observed.

articleTitle: Two-dimensional photonic crystals: waveguides and guided resonance
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: A general designing procedure is introduced that allows for any given photonic crystal slab, to create an appropriate waveguide structure that possesses single-mode bands with large bandwidth and low dispersion within the photonic band gap below the light line. The procedure consists of two steps: i) designing a conventional dielectric waveguide that is optimally phase matched with the band gap of the photonic crystal slab; and ii) embedding the dielectric waveguide into the photonic crystal in an appropriate way such that the edge states are eliminated and single mode propagation is ensured. This procedure produces waveguide structures with large bandwidth of single mode and lossless propagation, and creates dispersion relations that are essentially linear over most of the guiding bandwidth.

articleTitle: Amplitude noise on supercontinuum generated in microstructure fiber: measurements and simulations
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: Supercontinua generated in microstructure fiber can exhibit significant excess amplitude noise. We present experimental and numerical studies of the origins of this excess noise and its dependence on the input laser pulse parameters.

articleTitle: Photonic band-gap fiber: fiber of the future?
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: We briefly review the state-of-the art in photonic band-gap fibers. Recent reduction in attenuation to 13 dB/km demonstrates the potential of these hollow-core fibers to provide low-loss and low-nonlinearity for a variety of applications including transmission fiber.

articleTitle: PMD mitigation by a fiber-based all-optical signal regenerator
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: PMD mitigation by an all-optical signal regenerator based on spectrum broadening and slicing using normal-dispersion fiber is numerically analyzed. It is shown that synchronous modulation in front of the regenerator significantly improves the performance.

articleTitle: Comparison of PMD sensitivity for different modulation formats
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: The polarization mode dispersion (PMD) sensitivity for different modulation formats is compared and discussed, including PMD tolerance for different modulation formats on the design of PMD compensators. In addition, the robustness of solitons to PMD is also discussed.

articleTitle: BER measurements of a 40Gb/s receiver with adaptive threshold using polarization scrambling
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: Polarization scrambling is proposed to quantify the penalties of polarization dependent effects in optical receivers. The results will be dependent on the relative speed of the polarization changes and the control circuits in the receiver.

articleTitle: Timing jitter in short-distance pulsed-analog optical fiber links
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: Investigation of the timing jitter generated by propagating high-power optical pulses through short lengths of optical fiber is presented. It is measured using the phase-encoded optical sampling technique. Comparisons are made between measured and simulated results.

articleTitle: Applications of importance sampling to PMD
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: Applications of importance sampling to polarization mode dispersion (PMD) statistics in optical fiber transmission systems are presented. Previous methods that uses Monte Carlo (MC) simulations concentrates on the largest PMD values that allows only low probability events to be simulated. In the new method, importance sampling biases MC calculations of concatenated birefringent sections so that first- and second-order PMD values occur thereby allowing rare PMD events to be simulated more efficiently. Importance sampled MC techniques therefore provide a natural and effective tool to assess PMD statistics and PMD-induced impairments in optical transmission systems at realistic probability levels.

articleTitle: Low-PMD fibers
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: Low-PMD fibers are fundamental for the engineering of very-high capacity optical systems. Effective PMD reductions may be achieved by spinning the fiber as it is drawn. This paper reviews the PMD properties of periodically-spun fibers.

articleTitle: A programmable second-order PMD emulator and precision PMD measurement system based on a variable Faraday rotator
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: We have proposed a programmable PMD Emulator and its measurement system based on a variable Faraday rotator. This emulator can generate two components of SOPMD, which measured by developed measurement system agree with the simulation.

articleTitle: Eye diagram evaluation in single mode fibers having polarization mode dispersion, polarization dependent loss and chromatic dispersion
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: We present analytical studies of output intensity fluctuations of systems having PMD, PDL and CD. Analytical expressions for autocorrelation functions are derived. Results applied to different modulation formats lead to analytical evaluations of eye diagrams.

articleTitle: CO/sub 2/-laser-based RF frequency reference
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: The aim of the paper is to obtain an RF beat signal that has a stability similar to that of the laser lines. The setup consists of a CO/sub 2/ laser that uses two different isotopes of C and or O that oscillates at two optical frequencies in a single very high Q optical cavity. The output is mixed on a wideband photomixer to produce RF power at the difference frequency.

articleTitle: Pulse switching and compression in out-of-phase superimposed linear-nonlinear grating
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: Propagation of ultrafast pulses in a different kind of nonperiodic system is analyzed. Both layers of the structures being analyzed are considered to exhibit Kerr nonlinearity. The transmittance and reflectance characteristics of the proposed structures are investigated. When the out-of-phase linear grating is large enough to cause a significant built-in reflectance, the transmittance reveals an interplay between-built-in and intensity-dependent grating behavior. Pulse shapes in the presence of an out-of-phase linear grating are also determined. Pulses exhibit compression, reshaping and high-amplitude multi-peak oscillation effects depending on the length of the device.

articleTitle: Nonlinear photonic crystals in lithium niobate
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: This study demonstrates the idea of a 2-D photonic crystal by poling a wafer of lithium niobate with a hexagonal pattern. The fabricated crystal is used in performing experiments on 2nd, 3rd, and 4th harmonic generation. The peak conversion efficiencies of > 80% for SHG using picosecond pump pulses and conversion efficiencies of 10/sup -4/% for third and fourth harmonic generation using low power picosecond pulses are measured. In addition, the first observation of type II sum frequency generation in a periodically poled material is successfully made. This shows that 2D NPCs are ideal for multiwavelength harmonic generation. Problems on the intensity of the interacting waves and the effective nonlinearity are solved to realize multiwavelength harmonic processes.

articleTitle: Photonically assisted arbitrary millimeter waveform generation
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: We present cycle-by-cycle generation of broadband burst and continuous millimeter waveforms through a direct space-to-time optical pulse shaping technique. We generate arbitrarily phase- and frequency-modulated waveforms through fast optical-to-electrical conversion of tailored optical pulse sequences.

articleTitle: Polarization-modulated PSP transmission technique
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: A simple technique to improve the performance of the principal state of polarization (PSP) transmission technique by modulating the state of polarization (SOP) of the input optical signal at the clock frequency is proposed. It is demonstrated that the performance of the transmission could be significantly improved by modulating the signal's polarization. The result show that the proposed technique could improve the receiver sensitivity up to 1 dB, by transforming the NRZ signal into RZ signal, when differential group delay (DGD) was smaller than 80 ps. The technique also improved the performance of the PSP transmission under the higher-order polarization mode dispersion (PMD) environment.

articleTitle: Spun fibers for low PMD: understanding of fundamental characteristics
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: PMD reduction by fiber spinning is studied using coupled-mode theory. Fundamental characteristics of the spun fibers are examined. Some practical design issues are addressed.

articleTitle: Nonlinear optical studies of photonic crystal waveguides
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: This paper reports on nonlinear optical investigations of 2D photonic crystals etched into GaAs/AlGaAs waveguides by means of second-harmonic generation (SHG) from the surface of the samples. 130-fs laser pulses from a tunable Ti:sapphire source at 800 nm and from an optical parametric oscillator in the range 1.4 to 1.6 micron have been chosen to excite SH signals in reflection and diffraction directions. The measured angles of diffracted second-harmonic beams agree with those predicted from nonlinear diffraction conditions. The intensities of the reflected and diffracted SH signals are measured by varying the angle of incidence, input polarization and wavelength. Their observed behavior reflects the GaAs crystalline symmetry and the photonic crystal structure, respectively. Moreover, the measured high diffraction-to-reflection intensity ratio suggests the possibility of tailoring the nonlinear response using diffraction modes.

articleTitle: GHz waveform generation via direct space-to-time optical pulse shaping and dispersive stretching
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: We demonstrate a direct space-to-time optical pulse shaping technique for generation of GHz electromagnetic waveforms. Frequency-modulated optical pulse sequences are stretched in 5.5 km of single-mode fiber and converted to electromagnetic waveforms via fast optical-to-electrical conversion.

articleTitle: Investigations of quantum interference control in semiconductors for carrier-envelope phase measurements
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: Using two harmonically related pulse trains, we perform an experimental viability study that demonstrates the possibility of employing quantum interference control in semiconductors to detect the carrier-envelope phase evolution of a single octave-spanning pulse train.

articleTitle: Design of high-Q photonic crystal optical cavities through group-theoretical and Fourier space analyses
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: Group-theoretical and Fourier space analyses are used to design low loss photonic crystal cavities. Experimental results verifying the group theory predictions are presented, along with finite-difference time-domain calculations of recent designs with predicted quality factors exceeding 1/sup 5/5.

articleTitle: Micrometer-resolution long-distance measurement using a femtosecond frequency comb
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: This paper reports on the development of an ultrahigh accuracy distance meter (femtosecond-comb distance meter (FCDM)) with a simple setup and reliability for a practical measurement using a broad and stable femtosecond frequency comb. The distance meter is expected for a length standard as well as industrial applications. In this study, a 2-/spl mu/m uncertainty in the FCDM by using 10-GHz beat frequencies is achieved.

articleTitle: Femtosecond laser stabilization: time and frequency domain applications
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: Reducing noise in femtosecond laser systems becomes increasingly important as new applications are developed demanding improved levels of performance. Current stabilization techniques and applications from frequency metrology to coherent pulse synchronization will be discussed.

articleTitle: Increasing mean DGD measurement accuracy using second order PMD statistics
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: We propose an independent measure of the mean DGD using the statistics of the second order PMD. Numerical analysis and experiment indicate that this measurement technique reduces the measurement uncertainty.

articleTitle: 2-D photonic crystal microcavities
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: Summary form only given. We have recently developed photonic crystal nanocavities and lasers from both InGaAsP quantum well and InGaAs/GaAs quantum dot materials. We have explored the design compromises for developing high-Q cavities and developed new geometries for sensitive low-threshold optical switches and spectroscopy sources. In this talk, we will review the design, fabrication and characterization of optical cavities defined within photonic crystals.

articleTitle: Optical confinement of envelope wavefunctions in photonic crystal heterostructures
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: The optical confinement of envelope wavefunctions in photonic crystal heterostructures was studied. Coupled mode theory was used to calculate the states of 2D photonic crystal heterostructures (PCHs) consisting of a core photonic crystal (PC) embedded in a cladding PC. The core consists of larger-size coupled microcavities or waveguides and the cladding comprises smaller size elements. The photonic dispersion of each sub-lattice in the vicinity of the band edge was modeled using the effective propagation constants of the PC elements and the coupling constants between nearest neighbors. The calculated near field patterns of the two highest-order supermodes in a VCSEL-based PCH are presented. Confinement of the envelope functions to the PCH core arises due to the fact that the core modes lie in the forbidden gap of the PCH cladding. The lowest loss (out-of-phase) mode is always confined, whereas the confinement of lower order ones depends on the chosen parameters.

articleTitle: A novel matrix formulation for the propagation of modulated light in birefringent optical systems
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: The propagation of modulated light in birefringent optical systems is studied via a novel 4/spl times/4 time-dependent matrix. Using this formulation, the outcome of any linear operation on the output instantaneous Stokes vector can be fully characterized with only a few measurements.

articleTitle: Modes and their transitions in microstructured optical fibres
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: Microstructured optical fibres (MOFs) have modes which always have complex /spl beta/ values, blurring the distinction between guided and leaky modes. We divide them into localized and extended types, establishing the existence of clear transitions between them.

articleTitle: Impact of photodiode nonlinearities on optical to microwave frequency conversion
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: We present an overview of photodetector nonlinearities and their impact on generating spectrally pure electrical signals. Measurement techniques and various nonlinear observations will be reviewed and discussed.

articleTitle: Generation of continuous millimeter and sub-millimeter waves using photonic techniques
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: Recent progress in the photonic generation of high-frequency signals in the millimeter-wave (MMW) and submillimeter-wave (SMMW) regions is reported. Optical MMW signal sources based on semiconductor laser diodes (LDs) are described. Ultrafast photodiodes called uni-traveling-carrier photodiodes (UTC-PDs) and the enhancement of their output power by adding a matching circuit to the PD are explained. The integration of the PD with planar antennas for free-space applications such as transmitters in millimeter-wave wireless links and local oscillators in radio-astronomy receivers are shown.

articleTitle: PMD mitigation and receiver optimization to reduce PMD influence
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: The statistical distribution of the polarization mode dispersion (PMD) in a recirculating loop has been investigated and an analytical expression of the accumulated differential group delay (DGD) has been derived. It was found that the accumulated PMD-vector evolves spirally through Stokes space and the accumulated DGD becomes uniformly distributed as the number of circulations increases. The expectation value of the DGD increases linearly with the number of circulations through the loop, in contrast to a straight line transmission link, where the expectation value of the DGD grows as the square-root of the link length.

articleTitle: Maximization of supercontinua in fibers by using double pulses and polarization effects
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: Maximation of supercontinua (SC) in fibers are demonstrated by presenting 2 ways to increase the SC width at the same pulse energy and the fiber length. The first is by using a double pulse technique and the other is by the exploiting polarization effects.

articleTitle: Microstructured optical waveguides: so complex yet so simple
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: We propose a simple physical model that predicts spectral resonances of a class of microstructured optical waveguides consisting of high-index inclusions surrounding a low-index core. These resonances are largely determined by the geometry of individual high-index inclusions.

articleTitle: Photonic frequency synthesis and control with whispering gallery mode microresonators
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: Experimental and theoretical studies of electro-optical tunability of whispering gallery modes (WGMs) in high-Q monolithic lithium niobate resonators and their applicability for light modulation and filtering are reported. Properties of an optoelectronic microwave oscillator (OEO) based on an WGM LiNbO/sub 3/ resonator are discussed.

articleTitle: Absolute frequency measurements of acetylene-stabilized diode laser frequency standards
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: Two 1.5 /spl mu/m semiconductor laser frequency standards have been developed, based on Doppler-free /sup 13/C/sub 2/H/sub 2/ spectra. Preliminary absolute frequency values obtained using a combination of femtosecond-comb and passive comb systems will be presented.

articleTitle: Automatic wide range PMD compensator applicable to terrestrial installed fibers
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: The automatic PMD compensator using a polarizer and a Faraday rotator-based polarization controller with low-frequency-band monitoring was applied to an installed-terrestrial system with 350-km single-mode fibers. The compensator produced long-term stable operation for 40-Gbit/s channels.

articleTitle: Power capacity of hollow Bragg fibers, CW and pulsed CW sources
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: The power capacity and failure mechanisms for an emerging type of high power radiation guides - hollow photonic Bragg fibers (PBF) are investigated. CW and pulsed radiation are considered in the study assuming continuous operation of the laser source.

articleTitle: Scattering method calculation of the electromagnetic properties of two-dimensional photonic crystal slabs and waveguides
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: Theoretical studies on two-dimensional photonic crystal (PC) slabs are presented. A scattering matrix approach which allows a complete modeling of the electromagnetic properties of structures made of layers of dielectric materials with planar periodicity. The slab structure consists of a triangular lattice of air holes drilled through an InP suspended membrane. Band structures and inverse quality factor variation of the modes are calculated. The effect of membrane thickness or the air-filling factor are also studied. The method is shown to be a powerful tool for the analysis of guided and quasi-guided (resonant) modes in PC slabs of finite thickness either suspended in air or on a substrate.

articleTitle: Trapped ion optical frequency standards and metrology
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: Forbidden transitions in single laser-cooled trapped ions provide highly stable and accurate references for optical frequency standards. This paper describes work on strontium and ytterbium ion optical frequency standards currently under development at NPL.

articleTitle: Fabrication and characterization of the oxide-cladding-type AlGaAs-based photonic-crystal slab waveguides sandwiched between partially oxidized ridge waveguides
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: The paper reports of the fabrication and transmission characterization of the oxide-cladding- (OC) type photonic crystal (PC) slab waveguides (WG). By designing the PC-WG structure sandwiched between conventional ridge WGs and examining experimentally the oxidation, which often causes a strain-related fabrication trouble, the strain-free OC-PC WGs was successfully fabricated. Subsequent transmission characterization demonstrated the good property of the OC-PC waveguides and proved the validity of the fabrication technique.

articleTitle: Optical phase coherent locking of a 1550-nm mode-locked source to an optical atomic clock's fs comb
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: We have obtained optical phase coherence between a 1550-nm mode-locked diode laser and a 800-nm femtosecond frequency comb used in an optical atomic clock.

articleTitle: Photonic crystal enhanced optical interconnects
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: Progress toward integrated, highly functional optical interconnects that could operate at high data rates with much lower overall costs is presented. These integrated solutions are based on high index contrast planar lightwave optical waveguides, micro-resonators and one-dimensional (ID) photonic crystals.

articleTitle: High-index-contrast bend structures for microphotonics
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: Summary form only given. Bending or redirecting light beams is a crucial enabling function for passive integrated optical circuits. The efficiency and scaling properties of bends control the size and, therefore, the practicality of optical integration. In this talk, a review and comparison of the various design options for fabricating high-efficiency bends in high-index-contrast, integrated optical materials. Bend or "turning" designs using measured results with devices fabricated in the silicon-on-insulator material system are illustrated. The computational work has typically been done using FTDT. Particularly, this study compares two types of 90° bending mirror over a range of dimensions for using simulation and experiments. Results show that etched turning mirrors, which are also one of the earliest solutions to 90° bends, are one of the easiest and most efficient to implement. More advanced active devices for angular deflection are also examined and discussed.

articleTitle: Measuring component DGD using polarized fixed frequency components and monitoring the DOP
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: We propose two techniques to measure the DGD of components by scrambling the fixed polarized optical frequency components and measuring the resulting minimum degree-of-polarization.

articleTitle: Femtosecond metrology
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: Possibilities of frequency combs generated by femtosecond lasers in high precision spectroscopy on atomic hydrogen was explored at the 10/sup -14/ level. Fundamental tests of the fs frequency comb technique were done. Further applications arise in the time domain where the phase between the carrier and the envelope of a pulse can now be determined, allowing the production of isolated XUV attosecond pulses.

articleTitle: Disorder in 2D photonic crystals: modification of transmission and photonic minibands
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: The effect of radius disorder on complete and incomplete photonic band gaps are investigated. The incomplete gap of a two-dimensional hexagonal photonic crystal of air cylinders are considered for the TM electromagnetic modes. It was found that the introduction of disorder into a photonic crystal leads to modification the transmission spectra. For the complete photonic band gap with TE polarization, the spectra was found to be less sensitive to the disorder and that a critical ordering is required before transmission changes. The influence of random vacancies was also investigated.

articleTitle: Optical add/drop filter by contra-directional coupling between photonic crystal waveguides
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: The design, fabrication, and characterization of an optical filter based on a contra-directional photonic crystal waveguide coupler are presented. The efficient wavelength-selective operation is demonstrated, which is in good agreement with the theoretical results.

articleTitle: Gigahertz femtosecond lasers for optical frequency metrology
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: Femtosecond lasers with repetition rate around 1-GHz have several advantages for optical frequency metrology. A state-of-the-art review emphasizing the recent development of a 433-MHz Cr: forsterite laser and a 1-GHz continuum-generating Ti:sapphire oscillator is given.

articleTitle: Optical bistability in nonlinear photonic crystal systems
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: Using an analytical theory and detailed computational experiments, we predict surprising optical bistability behavior in various photonic crystal systems.

articleTitle: Equifrequency surfaces in a two-dimensional GaN photonic crystal for second-harmonic generation with tuning range
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: The equifrequency surface plot is demonstrated as a powerful tool in obtaining the angular geometries that maintain quasi-phase matched (QPM) conditions for enhanced SHG with extended tuning range. These results are promising for the practical realisation of nonlinear frequency conversion devices based on GaN and related materials.

articleTitle: Octave-spanning lasers and single-cycle pulse synthesis
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: An octave-spanning, prism-less Ti:sapphire laser is demonstrated based on double-chirped mirror pairs. The Ti:sapphire laser synchronized to a 30 fs Cr:forsterite laser using balanced cross-correlation. A residual timing jitter of a tenth of an optical cycle, i.e. 300 attoseconds is achieved.

articleTitle: Quantum-limited timing jitter in actively modelocked lasers
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: The quantum-limited timing jitter of actively modelocked lasers is set by the balance between amplified spontaneous emission and restoring forces provided by modulation and optical filtering. We present theory and experimental results for a fiber laser and an external-cavity semiconductor laser. We also show a scheme for reducing timing jitter using GVD and phase modulation.

articleTitle: Link design and networking issues related to PMD
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: We show how to handle polarization-mode dispersion (PMD) in opaque and transparent networks with and without mitigation and including protection. Both the statistical nature of PMD and the manufacturing process accuracies have to be considered.

articleTitle: Nonlinear responses of 2D photonic crystal waveguides
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: This paper focuses on the third order nonlinear response of 1D waveguide modes, and how they nonlinearly couple to 0D localized photon states. A complete analytic treatment of this problem, that allows for a complex third order susceptibility and downstream, nonresonant scattering, suggests that optical bistability should be achievable at average power levels of only a few milliwatts. Furthermore, appropriately designed waveguides can exhibit strong optical limiting behaviour as shown by experimental results. This saturated transmission of pulses from an optical parametric oscillator is due to two-photon absorption in the silicon slab used to fabricate the waveguide.

articleTitle: Nonlinear magneto-optical effects in magneto-photonic microcavities
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: Quadratic and cubic nonlinear magneto-optical effects are observed in the one-dimensional magneto-photonic microcavities (MC). Magnetization-induced second-harmonic and third-harmonic generations are studied in magneto-photonic MC with microcavity spacer formed from Bi-substituted yttrium-iron garnet.

articleTitle: Measuring jitter: timing and amplitude, uncorrelated and correlated, absolute and residual
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: We present theory, simulations, and experiments validating direct and mixing-based spectral methods for extracting six jitter parameters (total, uncorrelated, and correlated; timing and amplitude) of a pulse train. Absolute and residual noise are discussed.

articleTitle: The Brownian bridge method - an alternative to importance sampling and a tool for the study of the spectral dynamics of PMD
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: The Brownian bridge method is described along with its applications to the study of polarization mode dispersion (PMD) in fiber-optic systems. This method offers an alternative to importance sampling in numerical computations and it constitutes an extremely powerful tool in the study of the spectral statistics of PMD.

articleTitle: Enhancement of second harmonic generation due to quasi-phase matching condition in a GaN-based one-dimensional photonic crystal
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: This paper reports measurements of the the giant second harmonic generation (SHG) enhancement of a 1D thin-film GaN-based photonic structure. The extraordinary enhancement has been obtained in specular reflection when the angular configuration satisfies the quasi-phase-matching (QPM) conditions, i.e. when both the fundamental and SH fields are resonant with radiative Bloch modes.

articleTitle: Coupling issues in strongly confined nanophotonic waveguides
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: We present several devices to couple light efficiently into strongly confined nanophotonic-waveguides (surface fibre coupler, compact spot-size converter). These devices are fabricated in SOI using deep-UV lithography.

articleTitle: Octagonal photonic quasicrystal based add-drop filter
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: This paper presents a numerical study and design of a ring resonator add-drop filter based on a photonic quasicrystal. The design consists of an octagonal lattice of high index (n = 2.9) dielectric rods in air. This structure is known to possess a complete photonic bandgap for the TM polarisation over a wide range of refractive indices of the rods. The FDTD method is used to calculate the spectral response of a quasicrystal, waveguides, resonators and add-drop filter based on these building blocks. The proposed structure demonstrates a reasonable efficiency, opening the possibility for further optimization and practical realization.

articleTitle: Testing the foundations of special relativity cryogenic optical resonators
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: A new Michelson-Morley (MM) experiment was performed by a one-year comparison of the frequencies /spl nu//sub x/ and /spl nu//sub y/ of two lasers stabilized to crossed cryogenic optical resonators (COREs) at 10.64 nm. The developed laser stabilization scheme uses automatic beam positioning to compensate for cryostat movements. Data were analyzed within the general standard model extension (SME).

articleTitle: Opto-electronic carrier-envelope-phase detection
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: The possibility of detecting the carrier-envelope (CE-) phase by measuring directly the inversion in a two-level medium after excitation with an off-resonant few-cycle laser pulse is demonstrated by numerical simulations.

articleTitle: One- and two-photon lasing in an organic 2-D photonic band gap structure
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: Optically pumped organic lasers are fabricated onto a 2-D photonic band gap structure. Lasing occurs at the band-edge or in the band gap in excellent agreement with our modeling. Furthermore, frequency up-converted lasing is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Progress in generation and applications of phase-stabilized, few-cycle pulses at MHz repetition rate in Vienna
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: The paper discusses on the generation and full characterization of 4-fs phase-stabilized pulses as well as their temporal carrier-envelope phase (CEP) jitter, first experimental demonstration of a phase-sensitive detector on a base of photoemission effect from a solid target, and generation of a self-phase-stabilized signal based on a difference frequency generation.

articleTitle: Optical clocks and low noise frequency synthesis using femtosecond lasers
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: We describe the role and performance of femtosecond lasers used in optical clocks. The femtosecond laser functions as a broadband, low-noise synthesizer that converts optical frequencies to the microwave domain, and vice versa.

articleTitle: Jones matrix and joint probability distributions for third order PMD
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: A Jones matrix model describing polarization mode dispersion taken to third order is presented. Further, simulated joint probability distributions for the three Stokes space components of the third order PMD vector are illustrated.

articleTitle: Supercontinuum generation in germanium-doped fibers and comparison with microstructured fibers
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: This paper studies the supercontinuum generation in germanium-doped silica fibers (highly nonlinear dispersion shifted fiber) as compared with microstructured fibers. Numerical simulations were performed and it was found that the physical effects responsible for continuum generation are soliton formation, self-frequency shifting, time-delayed Raman and four-wave mixing that exists in both structures in the 800 and 1550 nm range. It is therefore concluded that highly nonlinear fibers has the potential for extreme supercontinuum generation as the microstructured fibers.

articleTitle: PMD mitigation and receiver optimization to reduce PMD influence
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: The efficiencies of a number of passive and active PMD mitigation techniques are quantified. The implications of using a fixed receiver decision point (threshold and timing) are also discussed and compared with an adaptive receiver.

articleTitle: Supercontinuum generation under higher-order mode excitation in a microstructured fiber
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: The paper reports on the generation of a supercontinuum whose spectrum is partly divided between fundamental and higher-order modes. The mechanism leading to the continuum generation and the resulting spectrum are found to depend critically on the combination of the excited modes. In particular, multimode four-wave mixing with large wavelength separation between the Stokes and antiStokes bands is observed. This effect could be advantageously used, e.g. for wavelength conversion.

articleTitle: Air-core photonic band-gap fibres without polarisation degeneracy
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: An air-core holey fibre design that supports a single, circularly symmetric, polarisation non-degenerate mode is presented. The mechanism through which polarisation nondegeneracy is achieved, the consequent advantages, applications and fabrication methods will be discussed.

articleTitle: Low-noise microwave oscillators based on high-Q sapphire dielectric resonators
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: Two almost identical 9 GHz oscillators were constructed, each characterised by approximately 500 mW of microwave power dissipated in the sapphire loaded cavity (SLC) resonator. The phase locking of the 'slave' oscillator to 'master' required for the phase noise measurements, was accomplished by altering the level of microwave power dissipated in the SLC resonator of the 'slave' resonator. The spectral density of phase fluctuations of both oscillators was measured with a dual-channel readout system calculating the cross-spectral density of voltage fluctuations between the channels in order to minimise the effect of uncorrelated fluctuations of the each channel on the resolution of spectral measurements.

articleTitle: Frequency metrology for wavelength division multiplexed optical fiber communications
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: Wavelength calibration is essential to ensure channel stability and characterize optical components for wavelength division multiplexed optical fiber communications. I will discuss the optical frequency metrology requirements, future trends, and our research in this area.

articleTitle: Group-velocity dispersion and deterministic PMD of modes in a hollow omnidirectional Bragg fiber
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: This articles demonstrates and discusses the group velocity dispersion and deterministic polarization mode dispersion in an omnidirectional photonic bandgap Bragg fiber (OPBF). Analysis of the mode's dispersion properties were obtained by a transfer matrix technique while PMD of the elliptically distorted OBPFs was calculated by using a Hamiltoninan formulation of Maxwell's equation in terms of transverse components of electromagnetic fields.

articleTitle: A fast and efficient finite-element solver for 2D and 3D photonic band-gap problems
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: Bloch-modes in 2D and 3D photonic crystals are calculated with fast and efficient finite-element codes. We present a detailed convergence-analysis of obtained solutions using multigrid algorithms and finite elements of higher orders.

articleTitle: Electrical equalization and error correction coding for optical channels
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: Adaptive Viterbi equalizer and DFE concepts for non-linear intersymbol interference (ISI) are presented. Iterative receivers for FEC and ISI ("turbo equalization ") allow to remove distortion loss in the electrical domain.

articleTitle: SOI 2D photonic crystals for microphotonic integrated circuits
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: We review recent achievements in fabrication of silicon-on-insulator 2D photonic crystals compatible with microelectronics processing will be reported. We first address the problem of radiation and propagation losses by quantitative measurements of transmission spectra for various designs of photonic crystal waveguides. In optimized structures record low propagation losses of 20 dB/cm are reported. Next we show the way to effectively couple the light from the fiber to high index microphotonic circuits and photonic crystals by proper design of mode converter and butt-coupler.

articleTitle: Femtosecond frequency comb measurements across the optical spectrum
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: We describe our application of frequency comb technology to extend knowledge of absolute optical frequency for stabilized laser sources at 194 THz (1.54 /spl mu/m), 445 THz (674 nm), and 474 THz (633 nm).

articleTitle: Photonic crystal fibers: putting new life into an old hat
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: The development of artificially microstructured materials known as photonic crystals has resulted in new thinking in fiber optics. Photonic crystal fibers use the unusual properties of the new materials to deliver previously unattainable optical performance.

articleTitle: The many colors of photonic bandgap fibers: theory, materials, processing, characterization and applications
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: Summary form only given. A fabrication method is introduced which enables the combination of two solid materials having dissimilar indices of refraction in a single fiber structure. This method involves the selection of optically distinct yet thermally compatible materials, a novel preform fabrication technique and fiber draw, and has led to the fabrication of the first optical transmission fiber that has lower losses than the materials that it is made of. The characterization effort of these novel structures is presented in light of the extensive theory design and modeling work that has been conducted at MIT and others. In particular the focus of this work is on direct reflection measurements of cylindrical bandgap fibers that corroborate the magnitude and position of the bandgaps as well as more recent results pertaining to fibers for high-power laser transmission. Other applications are also discussed.

articleTitle: A simple method for fabricating high-birefringence nonlinearly chirped Bragg grating as a PMD compensator
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: We proposed a simple method for fabricating high-birefringence nonlinearly chirped fiber Bragg grating by writing into a high-birefringence photosensitive tapered fiber through a linearly chirped phase mask. Its performance as PMD compensator is demonstrated experimentally.

articleTitle: Practical and detailed analysis of photonic crystal waveguides
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: A practical and detailed analysis of light propagation around a 90 /spl deg/C bend corner in a photonic crystal slab is presented. Transmision spectra of samples with different designs are compared for better understanding of the transmission efficiency and the losses. Points where the reflection occurs can be identified by Fourier transformation of the transmission spectrum. The fringe contrast of the Fabry-Perot modulation may also allow the evaluation of the losses in the waveguide by calculating the loss coefficient.

articleTitle: PMD in optical communication systems
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: The paper presents polarization mode dispersion (PMD) in optical communication systems. More particularly, it highlights certain key systems in dealing with PMD effects: monitoring, emulation, mitigation, compensation and PMD and polarization dependent loss (PDL) interactions.

articleTitle: Calculating microstructured optical fiber loss using the finite-difference time-domain algorithm
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: We demonstrate the calculation of loss in microstructured optical fibers using the finite-difference time-domain algorithm. The method uses direct modal propagation with longitudinal periodic boundary conditions. We compare the results to existing methods.

articleTitle: The mercury single-ion optical clock and a test of the stability of the fundamental constants
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: Summary form only given. Results of the measurements which compare the frequency ν/sub Hg/ of the /sup 199/Hg/sup +2/ S/sub 1/2/ (F=0) - /sup 2/D/sub 1/2/ (F=2, m/sub F/=0) optical transition to the SI second as realized at NIST are reported. Since the NIST time scale is calibrated with a cesium fountain primary frequency standard, the ratio of ν/sub Hg/ ( ≈ 10/sup 15/ Hz) to the cesium ground-state hyperfine splitting ν/sub Cs/ (≈ 9.2 GHz) is measured. These measurements show better reproducibility than 10 Hz at ν/sub Hg/, and constrain any possible variation of the ratio ν/sub Hg/ /ν/sub Cs/ to ± 7·10/sup -15/ yr/sup -1/.

articleTitle: Guiding light in colloidal photonic crystals
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: We analyze waveguiding in cylindrical structures in colloidal photonic crystals. We compare guides with air cores and raised-index cores in terms of mode shape and number of modes as a function of size.

articleTitle: Ultra-compact devices in photonic crystals: optical behaviour and semi-analytic models
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: An efficient and powerful method recently developed for calculating the transmission properties of photonic crystal waveguides to design an ultra-compact optical device that combines mode coupling in parallel waveguides and Fabry-Perot effects to reduce the coupling length and create a sharp spectral response. The general approach for joining multiple PC waveguide structures can be applied to study many different optical devices and coupling problems.

articleTitle: Octave spanning conventional geometry Ti:sapphire laser
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: We obtain direct stabilization of the laser offset frequency for a conventional geometry, octave spanning, Kerr-lens modelocked Ti:sapphire laser. Beam characteristics of the continuum are presented.

articleTitle: Pulse timing jitter suppression module using timing controlled optical feedback mechanism for GS-LD
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: Timing jitter suppressed optical pulse generator module is realized by using gain-switched laser diode with optical feedback timing control mechanism. 9.7-ps timing jitter deviations are easily suppressed less than 1-ps at the wide range repetitious rate between 500 MHz to 7 GHz.

articleTitle: Networking aspects of link PMD and its compensation
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: The paper presents the networking aspects of link polarization mode dispersion (PMD). Discussions are focused on the nature and reliability of optical networks, PMD of installed fiber infrastructures and techniques for PMD compensation.

articleTitle: Nonlinear photonic crystals: all-optical switching and gap solitons
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: We discuss a number of the nonlinearity-induced effects in two-dimensional photonic crystals with embedded nonlinear defects, such as bistable propagation, all-optical switching, resonant transmission through a bend, and spatial gap solitons.

articleTitle: Spectroscopy of second- and third-harmonic generation in silicon photonic crystals and microcavities
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: In this paper enhanced second- and third-harmonic generation (SHG and THG) is observed in one-dimensional photonic crystals and microcavities (MCs) formed from mesoporous silicon. The SHG and THG spectra measured in both frequency and wave-vector domains reveal two types of the resonant enhancement, namely, as the fundamental radiation is tuned across the photonic band gap edge and if it is in the resonance with the MC mode. The SHG and THG enhancements are observed also in coupled photonic-crystal microcavities, in which the electromagnetic interaction between coupling cavity spacers is controlled by the intermediate Bragg reflector. The eigenmodes of coupled MCs are split with spectral (angular) gap determined by the intermediate photonic crystal transmittance.

articleTitle: Carrier-envelope dynamics and stabilization of few-cycle laser sources
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: Analysis and investigations on carrier-envelope noise, generating mechanisms in mode-locked laser oscillators are discussed. Understanding of these mechanisms is an important prerequisite for building jitter-free clockworks for frequency metrology and applications in extreme nonlinear optics.

articleTitle: Time-stretch and wavelength-division sampling: photonic preprocessing techniques for ultrafast analog-to-digital conversion
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: The paper has outlined two novel applications of time-wavelength mapping techniques in analog-to-digital conversion. The general approach is to increase the performance of an electronic digitizer by optical signal reprocessing. Presently, the time-stretch technique appears to be the most promising in enabling ultra wideband analog-to-digital conversion with moderate resolutions.

articleTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: Presents the front cover, front matter, and table of contents from the conference proceedings.

articleTitle: Author index
publicationTitle: 2003 Digest of LEOS Summer Topical Meeting (Cat. No.03TH8701)
abstract: The author index contains an entry for each author and coauthor included in the proceedings record.
